item.title: Study Finds Americans Overestimate Harmful Behavior on Social Media
item.description: A study published in PNAS Nexus reports that Americans consistently overestimate how many social media users post harmful content online. Across three national studies involving 1,090 U.S. adults, participants believed large shares of users on platforms such as Reddit and Facebook engaged in toxic language or shared false news. item.title: Global Report Flags Rising Use of Digital Controls to Suppress Dissent
item.description: A 2025 report by the University of Rhode Island’s Center for Nonviolence and Peace Studies documents a global rise in what researchers describe as digital repression by governments. item.title: JP Conte: Five Things You Need To Successfully Build Strategic Partnerships [Promoted]
item.description: Private equity professionals often speak about returns, multiples, and exit timelines. JP Conte, managing partner of a San Francisco-based private equity firm and founder of family office Lupine Crest Capital, tends to speak about something else: relationships. Over a career spanning three decades — one that has seen his firm grow from approximately $100 million to $49 billion in assets under management — Conte has developed a distinctive philosophy about what makes partnerships succeed or fail.

item.description: The U.S. unemployment rate has been steadily rising since May, reaching 4.6% in November - the highest level seen since September 2021. item.title: Most Data Centers Are Located Outside Recommended Temperature Ranges
item.description: Data center placement influences electricity demand and cooling requirements, which are documented factors in energy system planning. An analysis by Rest of World found that a majority of the world’s operational data centers are located in climates outside the industry’s recommended temperature range. The analysis combined climate records from the Copernicus Climate Data Store with facility location data from Data Center Map, covering 8,808 operational data centers worldwide as of October 2025.
